citation_checks.quote: Among recent hybrids, Nguyen, Hoang, and Cheema [28] combined CNN and LSTM for RIS-NOMA channel estimation without addressing phase wrapping.
citation_checks.evidence: Abstract (OpenAlex/IEEE, CC BY): "This paper proposes a deep learning (DL)-based channel estimation method using a convolutional long-short term memory (CNN-LSTM) model for RIS-NOMA wireless communication systems". Full text (Ulster repository) contains no discussion of phase wrapping; phases are fixed: "we fix phase shift by generating fixed phase shifts in [0.01π, 0.02π]".

citation_checks.quote: LSTM recurrence thus captures structured inter-element spatial dependencies—analogous to PixelRNN for spatially ordered pixels [28].
citation_checks.evidence: Full text contains no mention of PixelRNN or pixels; in [28] the LSTM models time, not element order: "CNN can capture special features while LSTM can capture temporal features of time-series data" and "the features from CNN are fed into LSTM for decoding, and in turn extract the temporal correlation".

citation_checks.quote: 1-bit → 4.12°, 2-bit → 3.08°, 3-bit → 2.81° RMSE (continuous: 2.77°). Two-bit quantization recovers near-continuous performance, consistent with [38].
citation_checks.evidence: Same as above: [38] reports only 1-bit prototypes ("Both metasurfaces are phase-programmable with 1-bit coding.") and makes no 2-bit vs continuous comparison.
